1_incompressible_synthetic.result: REFUSED, enc_ret 0, error 18, 0 bytes out, 9,816 us before refusing

the_three_runs_that_settle_it.conclusion: synthetic data is not what the engine objects to: run 3 is synthetic and was accepted. Of the two explanations the earlier pair confounded - the source being generated, or its output exceeding the declared length - only the second survives. The engine refuses work whose output would not fit the length it was handed, and it refuses it by REFUSING rather than by overrunning or truncating: 0 bytes out, guards untouched.

measured_run_3.source_hash_significance: the camera's own fill and the host's generate_flat produce byte-identical data. Checked under emulation first and now confirmed live, which is what makes the demand figure above describe the data the camera actually encoded.
measured_run_3.calibration: the camera produced 283,648 B where the host encoder needs 264,752 - the camera is 7.1% above the host's optimal-per-tile Huffman estimate for this pattern. Any prediction built on the host encoder needs at least that much margin. One pattern, one run.

reasons: the host encoder does not need more than the declared length for this pattern, so the run did not put the limit under any pressure
the output stopped 91.0% below the declared length: the guards are unchanged because nothing reached them
verdict_on_run_3.note: this run was never a bound test and the criterion says so. Its value is the discriminator, not a verdict.

what_this_means_for_zero_copy.gained: the engine's response to work it cannot fit is a refusal before it writes anything. That is a far better property than the guard words could ever have shown, because a refusal is safe and an overrun is not.
what_this_means_for_zero_copy.NOT_gained: this does NOT authorise encoding in place over a frame's RAW. The refusal here happened with a source in one block and a destination in another, and produced no output. Whether the decision is made BEFORE writing begins or partway through is not established - and in place, a refusal partway through has already destroyed the RAW it was reading. ROADMAP's position stands: even if the hardware stops, in-place encoding may destroy the source first.
still_open: where the threshold is. Three points: 8.4% accepted, 30.3% accepted, 107.2% refused. A bisection would be needed to say the boundary is the declared length itself rather than something near it.
whether the refusal is a pre-flight estimate or a mid-encode abort. The 9,816 microseconds before refusing is the only clue, and it is one reading.
everything about read/write ordering in place.

an_operational_lesson_recorded_for_the_f.what_happened: after the power cycle the first preflight failed with the frame length reading 0x80E600 = 8,447,488 B instead of 0x318200. The camera had come back in UHD: SetMovRecSize 2->3, SetMovCinemaDNGQuality 0->4, SetMovFramerate 3->12.
an_operational_lesson_recorded_for_the_f.why: the project forbids `menu save`, so every menu value we set lives in RAM only and a power cycle returns to what is in flash. No earlier session power-cycled and then kept testing, so this had never shown up.
an_operational_lesson_recorded_for_the_f.the_rule: after ANY power cycle, re-apply SetMovRecSize 2, SetMovCinemaDNGQuality 0, SetMovFramerate 3 and verify, BEFORE arming anything. The probe caught it - it refused a frame that did not match its geometry - but it cost a clip and an arming.
an_operational_lesson_recorded_for_the_f.the_probe_behaved_correctly: kind was 2 and the LR was right; it was the length check that refused. A probe that had trusted the geometry would have handed a 3.1 MB tile plan to an 8.4 MB frame.
